messages.content: Cargo is an operations dashboard for the duty dispatcher of Westhaven, a fictional container port: a live 3D harbour, berths, containers, river traffic and security in one app.

Cargo (Westhaven Port Authority) is an Uno Platform single-project app at Cargo/Cargo.csproj (Uno.Sdk 7.0.0-dev.115, pinned in global.json; heads net10.0-desktop, net10.0-browserwasm, net10.0-android, net10.0-ios and net10.0-windows10.0.19041 for WinAppSDK). Cargo/Liveline/ is a vendored tide-chart control, folded into the app project. The unit tests (276, NUnit) live in the development repository, noknowscode/Cargo.

**Key files:**
- Cargo/App.xaml (+ .cs): the hosting builder, DI (the PortState store as a singleton, ScannerCamera, the five section view models), the route tree (Shell > Main > one view-less route per section; Security's zones, access and inspection tabs nest under security) and DefaultResponsiveLayout (Narrowest 0, Narrow 600, Normal 1000, Wide 1280, Widest 1600), which every {utu:Responsive} uses.
- Cargo/Domain/: PortData.cs (every figure, in memory, the design's picture of 20:58), BerthPlan.cs (berth rules, refusals, the optimiser), PortState.cs (the store: the clock and the berth desk) with its parts NavigationState, StageState, ScannerState, YardState, CrewChat, NeedsYouQueue and InspectionLog, and ShiftClock (the time arithmetic).
- Cargo/Presentation/: one view model per page and embedded panel (MainViewModel, OverviewViewModel, BerthsViewModel, CargoViewModel, FleetViewModel, SecurityViewModel, HarbourViewModel, NeedsYouPanelViewModel and their parts) and the views; MainPage hosts the header and the sections as x:Load panes in a Visibility region; ScannerOverlay is the container scanner.
- Cargo/Controls/: Harbour/ (HarbourScene, an SKCanvasElement with an orbit camera; HarbourRenderer and HarbourWorld draw the terminal), BerthMap (drag-to-assign), ContainerScanner (a box projected by hand from XAML shapes, with X-ray), TimelineLanes, YardMap, RiverMap.
- Cargo/Styles/: ColorPaletteOverride.xaml (the palette: every Simple theme role in Light and Default from the design's token table, the file Studio's Themes tab edits) and TypographyOverride.xaml (the type scale: sizes and weights of the semantic text styles, Bricolage Grotesque for Display, MonoFontFamily for figures).
- Cargo/Themes/: Styles.xaml (the app's text styles, based on the semantic ones, and its buttons and cards, based on the theme's tonal and filled buttons and the Toolkit cards), Layout.xaml (only what no theme token says: chip insets, page frames, the swatch), Generic.xaml (the tide chart's default style), Icons.xaml, MotionTokens.xaml; Tokens.cs resolves palette roles and App.xaml colours in code for the canvas and Skia scenes.

**Patterns:**
- MVVM with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, not MVUX: [ObservableProperty] public partial properties and [RelayCommand]. Views bind with x:Bind only, never {Binding}. View models hold states and the data's palette keys; the views pick brushes through static x:Bind functions (Presentation/Paint.cs and each view's code-behind), so every view model runs in the unit tests without a UI.
- WinUI traps kept: no required or init on XAML-activated types, bool to Visibility only through x:Bind, Uno-only APIs behind #if __DESKTOP__, arrays rather than collection expressions typed IReadOnlyList.
- The store raises separate signals (StructureChanged, PlanHourChanged, Ticked, HoverChanged, YardChanged) so a hover or a clock tick repaints rather than rebuilds.

**Navigation and theming:** Uno Navigation; the header navigates with uen:Navigation.Request, and jumps that start in the store set NavigationState.Section for MainViewModel to follow. Simple theme (SimpleToolkitTheme) plus the Uno Toolkit, Light and Dark: the palette is Styles/ColorPaletteOverride.xaml (ThemeColors.OverrideSource on the theme in App.xaml); pages and code use the generated role brushes (OnSurfaceBrush ink, OnSurfaceVariantBrush secondary text, BackgroundBrush page, SurfaceBrush panels, SurfaceVariantBrush sunk grounds, SurfaceInverseBrush with OnSurfaceInverseBrush for ink buttons and chips, PrimaryBrush/OnPrimaryBrush accent, ErrorBrush/ErrorContainerBrush needs-you, OutlineBrush/OutlineVariantBrush rules) through ThemeResource; the colours with no role (Navy and Water data, status fills and inks, maps, the 3D harbour, cargo classes, liveries, scanner materials) are App.xaml's own Light and Default dictionaries, the only hex besides the palette. Text is on the theme's type scale (Styles/TypographyOverride.xaml over DefaultFontFamily Archivo): role text styles are based on the semantic styles (DisplayLarge ... CaptionSmall), the colourless Type* styles use the same keys; spacing, radii and sizes are the theme's Space*, Radius*CornerRadius, ControlHeight* and IconSize* tokens (DefaultSpacing 8, DefaultCornerRadius 4). The scanner's stage is RequestedTheme Dark. No colour literal in C#, no hex, FontSize, FontFamily or CornerRadius literal in page XAML; the account menu's theme (System, Light, Dark) and Reduce motion are saved in local settings.

**What is simulated:** everything. There is no backend: the vessels, berths, containers, river crews and security events are constants in PortData, the clock runs on from 20:58 (DispatcherClock behind IClock), and the vessels' statuses stay as the design drew them. Berth assignments, confirmations, logged scans and crew messages live for the session only.

**Build:** dotnet build Cargo/Cargo.csproj -f net10.0-desktop -p:CargoTargetFrameworks=net10.0-desktop. CargoTargetFrameworks builds one head. Warnings are errors (Directory.Build.props). Hot Design and the App MCP are off in Debug on this SDK (Cargo.csproj says why). Debug-only CARGO_* environment hooks (Domain/DebugHooks.cs) open a section, a tab or the scanner for verification runs.

The app is built and running. The user may ask me to modify it.
